description: CHART 9 - Isotype / pictogram chart (advanced idiom). What Australia exports, by product type, FY2024/25. Each icon = 1,000 tonnes (rounded to whole icons, so products under 500 t get no icon); the exact tonnes and share of all 42,833 t exported are written at the end of each row. Why an isotype: icons make each product instantly recognisable and the counts easy to compare and remember (Week 5 workshop, Neurath's Isotype). Rows are sorted from largest to smallest. Transforms: share = tonnes / 42,833 x 100 (the report's export total); icons = round(tonnes / 1,000). The y encoding at the top is shared by both layers.

layer.description: Layer 1: the icons. sequence(1, icons + 1) makes a list 1..icons and flatten turns it into one row per icon; x = the icon's number places them in a line. The emoji is chosen by product type. Font size shrinks on narrow screens so icons don't overlap.

layer.description: Layer 2: exact tonnes and share at the end of each row (products with no icon get their label at the start). Meat's label is bold orange, the key fact.
